records.source: אֵ֜לֶּה מַסְעֵ֣י בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָצְא֛וּ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם לְצִבְאֹתָ֑ם בְּיַד־מֹשֶׁ֖ה וְאַהֲרֹֽן׃
records.gloss: These [are the] journeyings of [the] sons of Israel who went out from [the] land of Egypt by their armies, by [the] hand of Moses and Aaron.
pieces: These are the stages of the journey of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} when they came out of the land of Egypt by their divisions, led by Moses and Aaron.

L.1: These [are] the journeys of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, who went out from the land of Egypt by their armies, under the hand of Moses and Aaron.

R.1: This is the list of the places where the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} stopped on their journey after they came out of Egypt in their troops. Moses and Aaron led them.

decisions.choice: journeys: the stages of the march, from one camp to the next
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb "set out", which is repeated in every line of the list that follows (verses 5-49). Each "journey" is one move from a camp to the next, as in 10:12 ("by their stages"). The chapter looks back over the whole route from Egypt to the plains of Moab.

decisions.choice: by their armies: in ordered companies, like a marching army
decisions.reason: The word means a host or army. Israel left Egypt organized as a people under arms (Exodus 12:41, 51), and the tribes marched in their units (chapter 2; 10:14-28).

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses and Aaron: under their leadership
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" someone means through or under that person. Moses and Aaron led the people out at God's command.

decisions.choice: the stages of the journey (Balanced); the list of the places where they stopped (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the plural "journeys" means: one journey made in many stages. Literal keeps "journeys".

decisions.choice: armies (Literal); divisions (Balanced); troops (Readable)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Numbers for this word (10:14): each level uses its usual term for the army's units.

records.heading: The stages of Israel's journey from Egypt

records.source: וַיִּכְתֹּ֨ב מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶת־מוֹצָאֵיהֶ֛ם לְמַסְעֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־פִּ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְאֵ֥לֶּה מַסְעֵיהֶ֖ם לְמוֹצָאֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And wrote Moses their startings out by their journeyings at [the] mouth of Yahweh; and these [are] their journeyings by their startings out.
pieces: Moses wrote down the places they set out from, stage by stage, at {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s command. These are their journeys, listed by their starting points.

L.2: And Moses wrote down their starting places by their journeys at the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and these [are] their journeys by their starting places.

R.2: At {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s command, Moses wrote down the places where each part of their journey began. Here is the list of their journeys, place by place.

decisions.choice: at the mouth of Yahweh: Moses wrote the list at the LORD's command
decisions.reason: The phrase stands after "Moses wrote" and most naturally says that the writing itself was commanded, as other records were (Exodus 17:14; 34:27). It could also be read with "their journeys": the people moved from camp to camp at the LORD's command, as 9:18-23 says with the same phrase. Both are true of the journey; the question is only which the phrase points to here.

decisions.choice: their starting places: the places from which each stage began
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb "go out" and names a point of departure. Each line of the list names a place left and a place reached.

decisions.choice: the two halves reverse the order of the two nouns
decisions.reason: The verse says "starting places by journeys" and then "journeys by starting places". The crossing pattern rounds off the heading: what follows is a full record of the route, stage by stage.

decisions.choice: the places they set out from ... starting points
decisions.reason: Balanced uses two different expressions for the one Hebrew word so that the reversed order still reads naturally. Literal keeps "starting places" both times.

records.source: וַיִּסְע֤וּ מֵֽרַעְמְסֵס֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽרִאשׁ֔וֹן בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֛ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן מִֽמָּחֳרַ֣ת הַפֶּ֗סַח יָצְא֤וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּיָ֣ד רָמָ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And they set out from Rameses in the month the first, on [the] fifteenth day of the month the first; from [the] next day of the Passover went out [the] sons of Israel with a hand raised before [the] eyes of all Egypt,
pieces: They set out from Rameses on the fifteenth day of the first month. On the day after the Passover the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} marched out boldly in full view of all the Egyptians,

L.3: And they set out from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month; on the day after the Passover the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel went out with a raised hand before the eyes of all Egypt,

R.3: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} left Rameses on the fifteenth day of the first month, the day after the Passover. They marched out boldly, and all the Egyptians saw them go.

decisions.choice: the fifteenth of the first month, the day after the Passover
decisions.reason: The Passover lamb was killed on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month (Exodus 12:6, 18; Numbers 28:16). The firstborn of Egypt died that night, and Israel left the next day (Exodus 12:29-34, 51).

decisions.choice: with a raised hand: openly and boldly
decisions.reason: A raised hand is a sign of strength and confidence. Israel did not slip away as runaways but left in the open, as Exodus 14:8 also says.

decisions.choice: Rameses: a city in the eastern Nile Delta
decisions.reason: Rameses was one of the store cities that Israel had been forced to build (Exodus 1:11), and the first point of departure in Exodus 12:37.

decisions.choice: all the Egyptians
decisions.reason: "All Egypt" means the people of Egypt, who saw Israel go. Literal keeps "all Egypt".

decisions.choice: ends with a comma
decisions.reason: The sentence goes on into verse 4, which tells what the Egyptians were doing as Israel left. Readable closes the sentence here.

records.source: וּמִצְרַ֣יִם מְקַבְּרִ֗ים אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִכָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה בָּהֶ֖ם כָּל־בְּכ֑וֹר וּבֵאלֹ֣הֵיהֶ֔ם עָשָׂ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה שְׁפָטִֽים׃
records.gloss: and Egypt [were] burying those whom had struck Yahweh among them, every firstborn; and on their gods had done Yahweh judgments.
pieces: while the Egyptians were burying all their firstborn, whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had struck down among them. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had also carried out judgments on their gods.

L.4: and the Egyptians [were] burying those whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had struck down among them, every firstborn; and on their gods {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had carried out judgments.

R.4: At that time the Egyptians were burying all their firstborn, whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had struck dead. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had also brought judgment on their gods.

decisions.choice: the Egyptians were burying: what was going on as Israel left
decisions.reason: The verb form describes an action in progress. While Israel marched out boldly, the Egyptians were busy with their dead. The contrast shows who had been defeated.

decisions.choice: judgments on their gods: the LORD showed the gods of Egypt to be powerless
decisions.reason: The LORD had said he would carry out judgments on all the gods of Egypt (Exodus 12:12). The gods could not protect their people, even the firstborn of the royal house (Exodus 12:29).

decisions.choice: while ... / At that time
decisions.reason: Balanced joins the clause to the end of verse 3 with "while"; Readable, which ended verse 3 with a full stop, begins a new sentence.

records.source: וַיִּסְע֥וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵרַעְמְסֵ֑ס וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּסֻכֹּֽת׃
records.gloss: And set out [the] sons of Israel from Rameses and camped at Succoth.
pieces: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.

L.5: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.

R.5: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} left Rameses and camped at Succoth.

decisions.choice: set out ... and camped: one stage of the march
decisions.reason: From here to verse 49 each line has the same two verbs: they pulled up their tents at one place and pitched them at the next. The repeated form makes the list a record of the whole route, stage after stage.

decisions.choice: Succoth: the first stop after Rameses
decisions.reason: Succoth, "booths", was the first camp on the way out of Egypt (Exodus 12:37; 13:20). Its site is not known for certain.

decisions.choice: set out ... camped (Literal, Balanced); left ... camped (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps one fixed wording for every line of the list (verses 5-49), so that the reader hears the repetition of the Hebrew. Readable says "left", as in 21:11.

records.source: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִסֻּכֹּ֑ת וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ בְאֵתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר בִּקְצֵ֥ה הַמִּדְבָּֽר׃
records.gloss: And they set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, which [is] on [the] edge of the wilderness.
pieces: They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.

L.6: And they set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, which [is] at the edge of the wilderness.

R.6: They left Succoth and camped at Etham, where the desert begins.

decisions.choice: Etham, at the edge of the wilderness
decisions.reason: Etham is the second camp in Exodus 13:20, where the settled land ended and the desert began. Its site is not known.

records.source: וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מֵֽאֵתָ֔ם וַיָּ֨שָׁב֙ עַל־פִּ֣י הַחִירֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־פְּנֵ֖י בַּ֣עַל צְפ֑וֹן וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י מִגְדֹּֽל׃
records.gloss: And they set out from Etham and turned back to Pi-hahiroth, which [is] on [the] face of Baal-zephon, and they camped before Migdol.
pieces: They set out from Etham and turned back to Pi-hahiroth, which faces Baal-zephon, and they camped in front of Migdol.

L.7: And they set out from Etham and turned back to Pi-hahiroth, which [is] facing Baal-zephon, and they camped before Migdol.

R.7: They left Etham and turned back to Pi-hahiroth, across from Baal-zephon, and they camped near Migdol.

decisions.choice: turned back: the turn God ordered before the crossing of the sea
decisions.reason: Exodus 14:2 tells of God's order to turn back and camp before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, facing Baal-zephon. None of the three places can be located with certainty today.

decisions.choice: he turned back: the whole people spoken of as one
decisions.reason: The verb "turned back" is singular, between plural verbs. The people are spoken of as one body for this single move; the sense is that they all turned back.

records.source: וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י הַֽחִירֹ֔ת וַיַּֽעַבְר֥וּ בְתוֹךְ־הַיָּ֖ם הַמִּדְבָּ֑רָה וַיֵּ֨לְכ֜וּ דֶּ֣רֶךְ שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת יָמִים֙ בְּמִדְבַּ֣ר אֵתָ֔ם וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּמָרָֽה׃
records.gloss: And they set out from before Hahiroth and passed through [the] midst of the sea into the wilderness, and they went [a] journey of three days in [the] wilderness of Etham and camped at Marah.
pieces: They set out from Pi-hahiroth and went through the middle of the sea into the wilderness. After three days' travel in the wilderness of Etham, they camped at Marah.

L.8: And they set out from before Hahiroth and passed through the midst of the sea into the wilderness, and they went a journey of three days in the wilderness of Etham and camped at Marah.

R.8: They left Pi-hahiroth and walked through the middle of the sea into the desert. They traveled for three days in the Desert of Etham and camped at Marah.

decisions.choice: Hahiroth: a shorter form of Pi-hahiroth
decisions.reason: The name lacks its first part here. It is the same place as in verse 7, and "from before" means from the camp in front of it.

decisions.choice: passed through the midst of the sea: the crossing of Exodus 14
decisions.reason: The great rescue of Exodus 14:21-29 is told here in a single clause. The list keeps to the stages of the route.

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Etham and Marah
decisions.reason: The desert east of the sea is called the wilderness of Shur in Exodus 15:22, and here the wilderness of Etham, after the camp of verse 6. Marah, "bitter", was named for its bitter water (Exodus 15:23).

decisions.choice: Pi-hahiroth
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the full name used in verse 7, so that the reader can see it is the same place. Literal keeps the shorter form.

records.source: וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מִמָּרָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אֵילִ֑מָה וּ֠בְאֵילִם שְׁתֵּ֣ים עֶשְׂרֵ֞ה עֵינֹ֥ת מַ֛יִם וְשִׁבְעִ֥ים תְּמָרִ֖ים וַיַּחֲנוּ־שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And they set out from Marah and came to Elim; and at Elim [were] twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there.
pieces: They set out from Marah and came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there.

L.9: And they set out from Marah and came to Elim; and at Elim [were] twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there.

R.9: They left Marah and came to Elim. There were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees at Elim, so they camped there.

decisions.choice: Elim: an oasis after the bitter water of Marah
decisions.reason: Exodus 15:27 tells of the same springs and palm trees. The line breaks the list's pattern ("came to" before "camped") to remember the place where water was plentiful.

decisions.choice: so
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the water and shade are why they camped there, as the order of the Hebrew implies.

records.source: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵאֵילִ֑ם וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ עַל־יַם־סֽוּף׃
records.gloss: And they set out from Elim and camped by [the] Sea of Reeds.
pieces: They set out from Elim and camped by the Red Sea.

L.10: And they set out from Elim and camped by the Sea of Reeds.

R.10: They left Elim and camped by the Red Sea.

decisions.choice: a camp by the sea between Elim and the wilderness of Sin
decisions.reason: Exodus 16:1 goes straight from Elim to the wilderness of Sin; this camp is named only here. "Sea of Reeds" is the name of the sea of the crossing, but it is also used for the gulfs on either side of the Sinai peninsula (21:4). Here it probably names the western gulf, along which the route ran.

decisions.choice: the Red Sea
decisions.reason: As in 21:4: Balanced and Readable use the familiar name; Literal translates the Hebrew name, "Sea of Reeds".

records.source: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִיַּם־ס֑וּף וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּמִדְבַּר־סִֽין׃
records.gloss: And they set out from [the] Sea of Reeds and camped in [the] wilderness of Sin.
pieces: They set out from the Red Sea and camped in the wilderness of Sin.

L.11: And they set out from the Sea of Reeds and camped in the wilderness of Sin.

R.11: They left the Red Sea and camped in the Desert of Sin.

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Sin: where the manna was first given
decisions.reason: Israel reached the wilderness of Sin a month after leaving Egypt, and there the LORD sent quail and manna (Exodus 16:1-15).

decisions.choice: the Desert of Sin
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 16:1, Readable says "desert" for "wilderness" in a place name.

records.source: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִמִּדְבַּר־סִ֑ין וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּדָפְקָֽה׃
records.gloss: And they set out from [the] wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
pieces: They set out from the wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.

L.12: And they set out from the wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.

R.12: They left the Desert of Sin and camped at Dophkah.

decisions.choice: Dophkah: a camp named only in this list
decisions.reason: Dophkah and Alush (verse 13) stand between the wilderness of Sin and Rephidim, where Exodus 17:1 says only that Israel moved "by their stages". Their sites are not known.

records.source: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִדָּפְקָ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּאָלֽוּשׁ׃
records.gloss: And they set out from Dophkah and camped at Alush.
pieces: They set out from Dophkah and camped at Alush.

L.13: And they set out from Dophkah and camped at Alush.

R.13: They left Dophkah and camped at Alush.

decisions.choice: Alush: a camp named only in this list
decisions.reason: As in verse 12.

records.source: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵאָל֑וּשׁ וַֽיַּחֲנוּ֙ בִּרְפִידִ֔ם וְלֹא־הָ֨יָה שָׁ֥ם מַ֛יִם לָעָ֖ם לִשְׁתּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And they set out from Alush and camped at Rephidim; and not was there water for the people to drink.
pieces: They set out from Alush and camped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.

L.14: And they set out from Alush and camped at Rephidim; and there was no water there for the people to drink.

R.14: They left Alush and camped at Rephidim. There was no water there for the people to drink.

decisions.choice: Rephidim, where there was no water
decisions.reason: Exodus 17:1-7 tells how the people quarreled with Moses there and the LORD gave them water from the rock. The place was named Massah and Meribah. The list recalls only the lack of water.

records.source: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵרְפִידִ֑ם וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּמִדְבַּ֥ר סִינָֽי׃
records.gloss: And they set out from Rephidim and camped in [the] wilderness of Sinai.
pieces: They set out from Rephidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai.

L.15: And they set out from Rephidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai.

R.15: They left Rephidim and camped in the Desert of Sinai.

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Sinai: the camp at the mountain
decisions.reason: Israel camped before the mountain in the third month (Exodus 19:1-2) and stayed there almost a year, until the cloud lifted in the second month of the second year (10:11-12).

records.source: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִמִּדְבַּ֣ר סִינָ֑י וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּקִבְרֹ֥ת הַֽתַּאֲוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And they set out from [the] wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah.
pieces: They set out from the wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah.

L.16: And they set out from the wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah.

R.16: They left the Desert of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah.

decisions.choice: Kibroth-hattaavah: "graves of craving"
decisions.reason: The place was named for the people who died after craving meat and were buried there (11:31-34). Taberah (11:3) is not in the list; it may have been the name of an event near a camp rather than a camp of its own.

records.source: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִקִּבְרֹ֣ת הַֽתַּאֲוָ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בַּחֲצֵרֹֽת׃
records.gloss: And they set out from Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
pieces: They set out from Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.

L.17: And they set out from Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.

R.17: They left Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.

decisions.choice: Hazeroth: where Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses
decisions.reason: Israel moved on to Hazeroth (11:35), where the events of chapter 12 took place, and from there into the wilderness of Paran (12:16).

records.source: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵחֲצֵרֹ֑ת וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּרִתְמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And they set out from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
pieces: They set out from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.

L.18: And they set out from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.

R.18: They left Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.

decisions.choice: Rithmah to Ezion-geber: camps not named in the stories
decisions.reason: The camps from Rithmah to Ezion-geber (verses 18-35) do not appear in the stories of chapters 13-20, and most are named nowhere else. They seem to belong to the long years of wandering after the people refused to enter the land (14:33-34). The list does not mention the stay at Kadesh of 13:26; Kadesh comes only at verse 36. How these stops fit the story is not said.

records.source: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵרִתְמָ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּרִמֹּ֥ן פָּֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And they set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.
pieces: They set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.

L.19: And they set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.

R.19: They left Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.

decisions.choice: Rimmon-perez: a camp named only in this list
decisions.reason: Rimmon-perez is named only here and in verse 20. Its site is not known.

records.source: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵרִמֹּ֣ן פָּ֑רֶץ וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּלִבְנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And they set out from Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.
pieces: They set out from Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.

L.20: And they set out from Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.

R.20: They left Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.

decisions.choice: Libnah: a camp named only in this list
decisions.reason: This Libnah is named only here and in verse 21. It is not the town of Libnah in the south of Judah (Joshua 10:29), which lay far to the north of the wilderness.

records.source: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִלִּבְנָ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּרִסָּֽה׃

The text does not settle it.

decisions.choice: Aaron's death on Mount Hor
decisions.reason: The full account is in 20:22-29: Aaron went up the mountain with Moses and his son Eleazar, his priestly garments were put on Eleazar, and he died there. The list breaks off to remember him.

decisions.choice: the first day of the fifth month of the fortieth year
decisions.reason: Only here is the date of Aaron's death given. It places the end of the wilderness years: Israel left Egypt in the first month of the first year (verse 3), so almost forty years had passed.

decisions.choice: at the mouth of Yahweh: at Yahweh's command
decisions.reason: "Mouth" stands for what is spoken, as in verse 2. Aaron went up because the LORD told him to (20:23-26).

decisions.choice: told Aaron ... to go up
decisions.reason: Readable turns "at the LORD's command" into a clause of its own, which says the same thing in plainer words.

decisions.choice: the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho: the last camp
decisions.reason: The plains are the low land on the east side of the Jordan, opposite Jericho, where Israel camped from 22:1 to the end of the book (36:13). The phrase "the Jordan of Jericho" names the stretch of the river across from that city.

decisions.choice: across from Jericho
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where Jericho lay, on the other bank, as in 22:1. Literal brackets "at".

pieces: Their camp stretched along the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth to Abel-shittim in the plains of Moab.

L.49: And they camped by the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth as far as Abel-shittim in the plains of Moab.

R.49: Their camp spread out along the Jordan River all the way from Beth-jeshimoth to Abel-shittim, on the flat land of Moab.

decisions.choice: from Beth-jeshimoth to Abel-shittim: the length of the camp
decisions.reason: The two names mark the ends of the camp along the river. Abel-shittim, "meadow of acacias", is the Shittim of 25:1, from which Joshua later sent the spies (Joshua 2:1). Beth-jeshimoth lay nearer the Dead Sea (Joshua 12:3).

decisions.choice: they camped: the list ends without a further setting out
decisions.reason: This line has "camped" but no "set out". The journey stops here, where Israel stays until it crosses the Jordan (Joshua 3:1).

decisions.choice: Their camp stretched / spread out
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that "camped from ... as far as ..." describes the extent of the camp, not one more move.

decisions.choice: a new section: laws for entering the land
decisions.reason: With the journey over, the LORD speaks to Moses at the last camp. The commands from here to the end of the book (chapters 33-36) all look ahead to life in Canaan and are given at this place (36:13).

decisions.choice: across from Jericho
decisions.reason: As in verse 48.

records.heading: Drive out the people of the land

records.source: דַּבֵּר֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם כִּ֥י אַתֶּ֛ם עֹבְרִ֥ים אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן׃
records.gloss: Speak to [the] sons of Israel and say to them, when you [are] crossing the Jordan into [the] land of Canaan,
pieces: "Speak to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and tell them: 'When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,

L.51: "Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and say to them, 'When you cross over the Jordan into the land of Canaan,

R.51: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'You are going to cross the Jordan River into the land of Canaan.

decisions.choice: when you cross: an event close at hand
decisions.reason: The verb form describes the crossing as about to happen. The clause sets the time for the commands in verses 52-56.

decisions.choice: You are going to cross ...
decisions.reason: Readable makes the time clause a sentence of its own and picks it up at the start of verse 52 with "When you do".

records.gloss: then you will drive out all [the] inhabitants of the land from before you, and destroy all their figured [stones], and all [the] images of their cast [metal] you will destroy, and all their high places you will demolish.
pieces: drive out all the people who live in the land ahead of you. Destroy all their carved stones, destroy all their cast metal idols, and tear down all their high places.

L.52: then you shall drive out all the inhabitants of the land from before you, and destroy all their carved stones, and all their cast images you shall destroy, and all their high places you shall demolish.

R.52: When you do, force out all the people who live there. Destroy all their stone idols and their metal idols, and tear down all their hilltop shrines.

decisions.choice: drive out: take away the land from its people
decisions.reason: The verb means to dispossess: to make the people of the land leave so that Israel may hold it. The same root comes again in verse 53, "take possession".

decisions.choice: their carved stones: stones carved with images for worship
decisions.reason: The word names a stone with figures cut into it. Leviticus 26:1 forbids Israel to set one up and bow down to it.

decisions.choice: their cast images: idols made of molten metal
decisions.reason: These are images made by pouring melted metal into a mold, like the calf of Exodus 32:4.

decisions.choice: their high places: places of worship, often on raised ground
decisions.reason: A high place was an open-air shrine, often on a hill, with an altar and other objects of worship (Leviticus 26:30).

decisions.choice: hilltop shrines
decisions.reason: Readable says what a high place was. Literal and Balanced keep "high places".

records.source: וְהוֹרַשְׁתֶּ֥ם אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ וִֽישַׁבְתֶּם־בָּ֑הּ כִּ֥י לָכֶ֛ם נָתַ֥תִּי אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ לָרֶ֥שֶׁת אֹתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And you will take possession of the land and dwell in it, for to you I have given the land to possess it.
pieces: Take possession of the land and settle in it, for I have given the land to you to possess.

L.53: And you shall take possession of the land and live in it, for to you I have given the land, to possess it.

R.53: Take the land for your own and live in it. I have given it to you to be yours.

decisions.choice: take possession: hold the land as your own
decisions.reason: The verb is from the same root as "drive out" in verse 52. Driving out the nations and taking hold of the land are two sides of one act.

decisions.choice: I have given the land: Israel's claim rests on God's gift
decisions.reason: The land is Israel's because the LORD gives it (Exodus 6:8). It remains his, and Israel holds it under him (Leviticus 25:23).

decisions.choice: to you I have given
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "to you" first, as the Hebrew puts it for emphasis. Balanced and Readable use normal English order.

records.source: וְהִתְנַחַלְתֶּם֩ אֶת־הָאָ֨רֶץ בְּגוֹרָ֜ל לְמִשְׁפְּחֹֽתֵיכֶ֗ם לָרַ֞ב תַּרְבּ֤וּ אֶת־נַחֲלָתוֹ֙ וְלַמְעַט֙ תַּמְעִ֣יט אֶת־נַחֲלָת֔וֹ אֶל֩ אֲשֶׁר־יֵ֨צֵא ל֥וֹ שָׁ֛מָּה הַגּוֹרָ֖ל ל֣וֹ יִהְיֶ֑ה לְמַטּ֥וֹת אֲבֹתֵיכֶ֖ם תִּתְנֶחָֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: And you will inherit the land by lot by your clans; to the many you will make great his inheritance, and to the few you will make small his inheritance; to where goes out for him there the lot, to him it will be; by [the] tribes of your fathers you will inherit.
pieces: Divide the land among yourselves as an inheritance by lot, clan by clan. Give a larger inheritance to a larger clan and a smaller inheritance to a smaller one. Wherever the lot falls for a clan, that place will be its own. You are to receive your inheritance by your ancestral tribes.

L.54: And you shall take the land as an inheritance by lot according to your clans: to the larger you shall make its inheritance larger, and to the smaller you shall make its inheritance smaller. Wherever the lot goes out for it, there it shall be its [own]. By the tribes of your fathers you shall take your inheritance.

R.54: Divide the land by drawing lots, clan by clan. Give more land to the larger clans and less land to the smaller ones. Each clan will get the place where its lot falls. Divide the land by the tribes of your ancestors.

decisions.choice: take as an inheritance: divide among yourselves as lasting family property
decisions.reason: The verb form means to receive an inheritance for oneself, here by sharing out the land among the clans. An inheritance was property that stayed in the family.

decisions.choice: the lot and the size of the clan
decisions.reason: The same rule is given in 26:52-56. The lot decided where each group's land lay; the size of the group decided how much land it received.

decisions.choice: his inheritance, for him, to him: each clan
decisions.reason: The pronouns are singular and refer to each clan (or group) that receives a share, not to one man.

decisions.choice: its / a clan / each clan
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses "him" and "his" for the clan, as grammar requires. Each level says "it" or names the clan, since English uses "it" for a group.

decisions.choice: ancestral tribes / tribes of your ancestors
decisions.reason: "The tribes of your fathers" are the tribes named for Israel's ancestors. Literal keeps "fathers".

records.source: וְאִם־לֹ֨א תוֹרִ֜ישׁוּ אֶת־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָרֶץ֮ מִפְּנֵיכֶם֒ וְהָיָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תּוֹתִ֣ירוּ מֵהֶ֔ם לְשִׂכִּים֙ בְּעֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם וְלִצְנִינִ֖ם בְּצִדֵּיכֶ֑ם וְצָרֲר֣וּ אֶתְכֶ֔ם עַל־הָאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתֶּ֖ם יֹשְׁבִ֥ים בָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And if not you drive out [the] inhabitants of the land from before you, then will be [those] whom you leave of them as barbs in your eyes and as thorns in your sides, and they will harass you in the land in which you [are] dwelling.
pieces: But if you do not drive out the people who live in the land ahead of you, those you allow to stay will be like splinters in your eyes and thorns in your sides. They will make trouble for you in the land where you live.

L.55: But if you do not drive out the inhabitants of the land from before you, then those of them whom you let remain shall be as barbs in your eyes and as thorns in your sides, and they shall harass you in the land in which you are living.

R.55: But suppose you do not force out the people who live there. Then the ones you let stay will hurt you like a stick in your eye or a thorn in your side. They will cause you trouble in the land where you live.

decisions.choice: barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides: a constant source of pain
decisions.reason: Something sharp in the eye or the side never lets a person rest. The people left in the land would trouble Israel without end. Joshua 23:13 and Judges 2:3 take up the same picture.

decisions.choice: harass: press hard and act as an enemy
decisions.reason: The verb means to show hostility, to put someone in distress. The danger is both conflict and the pull of their worship (Exodus 23:33).

decisions.choice: But suppose you do not force out ... Then ...
decisions.reason: Readable splits the condition and its result into two sentences.

records.gloss: And it will be [that] as I intended to do to them, I will do to you.
pieces: And then I will do to you what I planned to do to them.'"

L.56: And it shall be [that] as I intended to do to them, I will do to you.'"

R.56: Then I will do to you what I planned to do to them.'"

decisions.choice: a warning: Israel would face what the nations faced
decisions.reason: The LORD planned to remove the nations from the land for their wrongs (Leviticus 18:24-25). If Israel let them stay and followed their ways, Israel too would lose the land (Leviticus 18:28; Deuteronomy 28:63).

decisions.choice: intended: planned, set in mind
decisions.reason: The verb means to think out or plan. What God planned for the nations he could also carry out against his own people.
